newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended sharply lower on Tuesday from the previous New York close on brisk overseas sales, particularly by the Swiss, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$356.80/357.30 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$358.30/70 close on Monday.

Swiss players had consistently sold gold in Asian trading hours, but the origins were unclear, with some dealers speculating on Swiss central bank sales and others noting the sales were on behalf of customers in the Middle East.
Traders earlier also reported selling from Australia.
Gold briefly touched $360 per ounce in intra-day trade, but the market ended directionless, with traders anticipating prices would drop below $356.50.
Physical demand was steady but dwarfed by selling pressure, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$16 lower at HK$3,297 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange society rose to +0.50 from its previous fix at nil.
"This could indicate that demand is up," one bullion trader said.
But players were disappointed by the lack of liquidity in the tael market and saw few arbitrage opportunities between the spot and tael market as many had already taken positions.
Tael gold was trading at a premium to the spot market, with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $357.50/358 per ounce.
